title: On Tearing the letter into four pieces
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：tear　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tear 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the cook ① tore the letter into four pieces before dawn, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② tears the letter into four pieces in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ tear the letter into four pieces at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ torn the letter into four pieces before — a line in the menu for September 1942 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Tearing the letter into four pieces before dawn, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ tear a strip from the old sheet in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Tear a strip from the old sheet at once and never mention it again.

By 1955 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ tears a strip from the old sheet before dawn every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ tore the letter into four pieces again when nobody else would.

⑩ To tear the letter into four pieces, my mother said in 1960, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody tears the letter into four pieces in public again and somebody must tear the letter into four pieces before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 撕裂（一般过去式 tore the letter into four pieces：1948 年厨子头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 撕裂（一般现在 tears the letter into four pieces：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 撕裂（不定式 to tear the letter into four pieces：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 撕裂（过去完成时 had torn the letter into four pieces：1942 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 撕裂（动名词 tearing the letter into four pieces 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 扯下（tear a strip from the old sheet：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去扯下从旧床单上扯下一条布）
G. v. 扯下（tear a strip from the old sheet：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 撕裂（后段两处：新来的客人照例 tears a strip from the old sheet，而母亲又一次 tore the letter into four pieces）

tear 意为“撕裂”，自那以后厨子当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 tears。
tear 意为“撕裂”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯撕裂把那封信撕成四片”，此处为不定式 to tear the letter into four pieces。
tear 意为“撕裂”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1955 年之前就有人撕裂过，故用过去完成时 had torn。
tear 意为“撕裂”，厨子说“撕裂把那封信撕成四片这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 tearing the letter into four pieces 作主语。
tear 意为“扯下”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去扯下从旧床单上扯下一条布”，should ever 之后用原形 tear a strip from the old sheet。
tear 意为“扯下”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻扯下从旧床单上扯下一条布（tear a strip from the old sheet at once），以后再也不要提起。
tear 意为“撕裂”，新来的客人每个日子都照例扯下从旧床单上扯下一条布，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 tears。
tear 意为“撕裂”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就撕裂把那封信撕成四片，用一般过去式 tore 叙述。
tear 意为“撕裂”，结尾那句是母亲 1960 年的话：要撕裂把那封信撕成四片，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 tear 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1948 the cook tore the letter into four pieces before dawn, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook tears the letter into four pieces in public whenever the canteen asks.
Tearing the letter into four pieces before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever tear a strip from the old sheet in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen tears a strip from the old sheet before dawn every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother tore the letter into four pieces again, and the canteen remembered that half.
